About the SIM PIN

Keep the SIM card locked with a PIN. At each start Android asks for it on its own screen, which can cover this one: Welcome cannot type it for you, and its warnings cannot be seen then. Type the PIN only after a normal start: nothing was updated since a start whose Welcome screen showed no warning, and you held no volume key while the phone started (that starts it without Antumbra\'s firewall). After an update, start once without the SIM card and check this screen first. If in doubt, do not type the PIN: restart the phone. Emergency calls may work without the PIN.
The SIM card is blocked after too many wrong PINs. Android asks for its PUK code on its own screen. Too many wrong PUK codes disable the card for good.

What your carrier sees

With Phone off, the cellular radio stays off, and your carrier gets nothing new from this phone. Android switches the radio on for an emergency call; your carrier then sees this phone, its SIM card and roughly where you are, as for any call.
With Phone on, the cellular radio is on from Start. While it is on, your carrier sees:
The cellular radio is off. Your carrier gets nothing new from this phone now. It keeps what it saw while the radio was on.
The cellular radio is on. While it is, your carrier sees:
Welcome does not know yet whether the cellular radio is on. While it is on, your carrier sees:
• your SIM card, and the name it is registered to
• this phone\'s identity (its IMEI); a new Wi-Fi address does not change it
• the cell towers the phone uses, and so roughly where you are, all the time
• who you call and text, when and for how long, and what you say in ordinary calls and texts
Calls and texts never go through Tor. Antumbra cannot hide them.
Mobile data goes through Tor: your carrier sees only encrypted Tor traffic, and that you use Tor.
Mobile data goes through Tor, over bridges. Plain bridges do not hide that you use Tor.
Mobile data is off: your Internet traffic does not pass through your carrier.
If your Wi-Fi is another phone\'s hotspot, that phone\'s carrier sees that you use Tor.
